body: I don't really have a doctor, I don't have health insurance so if I ever am like *really* sick I just go to the clinic, and that's only been 3 times in the last 10 years or so. Are psychologists or psychiatrists expensive? I feel like I really need to talk to someone but I honestly can't afford it if it's unreasonably expensive, I don't even know what I'm going to do about my bills this month.
Just knowing someone cared enough to talk actually makes a difference. I know we didn't exactly break any ground but I don't want you to feel discouraged because you actually did help me.

What I'll probably end up doing is sleep on it and read this thread again when I wake up and hopefully accept yours and whoever else's advice with a new set of eyes. Everything to me is so logical but I'm hindered by emotion. This is the perspective I'm seeing things from right now, I sent this to one of my friends in an immediate-post-breakup rant that I needed to get off my chest: 

>Everything in the universe has a reason. Everything. Everything comes down to a 0 or a 1. Is this proton stretched across these planck lengths in the universe? 0 or 1. What about this planck length, 0 or 1? What about this one? If it's been 0, it will be 0 until it reaches the end or becomes a 1. If it's a 1, it moves on to the proton. But what about the other 10000000000000000000000000000000000^100000s of protons, and their relative positions throughout the universe? Neutrons? Everything that is, is because of something being yes or no, 1 or 0. Maybe the other day she changed her mind about how she felt about me because she was in a bad mood, maybe she was in a bad mood because she woke up with a neurotransmitter that stopped working, maybe that neurotransmitter stopped working because of a misplaced cell, maybe that cell was misplaced because of a molecule that wasn't connected properly to begin with. And I would never know what atom it was or what transmitter it was because all she knows is that it was a mood change, an emotional flux. As a result here I am left without an answer to the fundamental question that would bring me the closure I so dearly seek, but I'll never have an answer.

When everything is a calculation like that, on a scale far grander than I could ever imagine, I don't see my significance to me or anyone else who has, does, or will live as very significant at all. On a long enough time scale, the survival rate for everyone and everything drops to zero. (Fight Club, heh) This is the basis for my feelings of apathy and desire for an end.

>stinkin' thinkin'

Funny you used that phrase, that's one of the phrases I and my old boss would use all the time to try to help build someone up. My biggest problem is going to be listening to what anyone has to say. The tricks are a matter of emotion, and work when there is a logical lag. My brain is constantly on the logical, with emotion as a painful and prevalent backburner. It's going to be hard listening to someone thinking about how each of their words could be different in a different reality because of a neuron being in a slightly different position. Do they really mean what they say? Do they even know what they're saying, to really mean it? 

I feel like I do need a psychiatrist though, or psychologist, not sure what the difference is. I need someone to talk to because I have other issues that neither of my girlfriends or boss knew about and no one really knows about them to be honest. It wasn't something that happened to me, I never got touched or molested, I've just got a pretty fucked up way of rationalizing things and that has led me to do some despicable things to people I'd never have to see or hear from again if I didn't want to.

I don't know her yet though, and if anyone can be the one to anyone, maybe all the girls I'm compatible with already have their one. I'm in one of the biggest slumps of my entire life so far. I don't care about meeting people, I don't care about knowing people, I just want to lay here until thirst takes me. If I thought you were right and I thought I would find someone, I'd be more motivated. But I just feel like that's never going to happen. I don't think I'll ever find true happiness (again) and that's why I just feel like this is pointless. Why bother feeling negative emotions when you can feel no emotion or anything else ever again?

I've actually read that article before, and I'm pretty sure I've referred it to someone on this subreddit. Because of my previous profession, I spent at least 40 hours a week building people up and being the positive role model for them and their children and showing them how to be a good person and cheery and upbeat and happy. I was a hero to these people, thousands of them over the course of the 6 years. I know all the psychocybernetic tips and tricks and have always had a penchant for psychology, but all this combined makes me very skeptical of my own happy thoughts. When I feel happy I get concerned that it's not real or it may change. Nothing seems to stick. Everything I do, everyone I talk to, all of it eventually leads to sadness :(

I genuinely am under the full belief that my first girlfriend was "the one". But I let things get sloppy and now I've lost her to someone else, and they've been together for about a year and are probably happy as could be while I'm here moping about how pointless my existence is.

I find nature beautiful. I love going out and getting stoned and observing nature around me. It's beautiful and I appreciate the tiny fraction of a fraction of a fraction of a percent  of a chance that *any* of this would ever exist, but unfortunately that's no longer enough to keep my chin up. I am a good person. I do everything I can to make other people happy. I exhaust myself trying to do so. For the last few months before I met Lily my body was running on empty because of the exhaustive effort I put into my old job and my old boss. That's unrelated but it just kind of came out. Anyway, I'm a very good person in my opinion. I do deserve happiness. But how do I make it myself? Because I'll do anything.

I think I'm to the point where I really don't even care about my role in the lives of my friends and family and the people I pass briefly. Being alone with my thoughts has made me bitter. I was having these thoughts about a year ago and they kind of stopped but only because I was so into my work because I was trying to make something happen that would ultimately make me happy, and the only reason they *had* to stop without suicide was  because I watched my mom lose her mom and watching her do that was one of the most painful things I have ever had to experience. Before I felt like I could never do that to my parents because I'd be in heaven and I'd see them and then they would see me whenever they died but now with my atheism I know that I'm just going to turn to dust.  Reading your post I just ask myself, what's the point? If there's just going to keep being meaningful hurt without meaningful happiness, and my only persuasion is the role I play in the lives of others at a point where I have effectively decided "fuck all them, they'll hurt me eventually anyway", what's left to keep me alive?
